memory_candidates.content: When a codebase carries an explicit consumer-side override flag (e.g. --allow-self-modifying in orchestrate), adding a sibling override is a mechanical 5-touch-point mirror in parse-command-args.sh (doc comment, default init, regex detection, FOCUS_PROMPT sed strip, export list) plus a threading chain command -> skill delegation context -> skill branch. The load-bearing invariant is that the override is NEVER passed to the predicate script: the predicate always computes and emits the honest verdict, and the flag is purely a consumer decision not to ACT on it, with a bypass notice logged whether or not the gate would otherwise have fired. Critically, a hazard's scope must be decomposed before a symmetric-looking flag is granted symmetric reach: for file_scope_collision, in_batch means two live co-dispatched agents editing the same files (a concurrent-write corruption hazard with a free bounded-retry remedy) while cross_batch means an idle out-of-batch task (a composition-judgment friction). Only the latter is a legitimate override target, so the flag's unqualified name must be contradicted explicitly in its help text.
